newsitem.title: USA: Mexico debtor union threatens to stop repayments.
newsitem.headline: Mexico debtor union threatens to stop repayments.

text.p: Mexicans burdened by bank debt will stop trying to make their payments next month if their demands for renegotiating loans are not met, a leader of a debtors' union said Tuesday.
Jose Maria Imaz, co-director of El Barzon, one of the country's largest protest movements, said indebted families were trapped by Mexico's high interest rates.

His union wants to renegotiate the debt in talks with the banks and the government. Otherwise the debtors' union will declare a moratorium on repayment on December 1, a step Imaz said could "shut down" Mexico's banking system.

Imaz said the debtors' union was encouraged earlier this year by a Mexican appeals court that ruled a bank had no right to enforce loan contracts because of legal questions about the privatization of the country's banks in 1991-92.
He spoke to reporters at a news conference at the offices of The Development Group for Alternative Policies in Washington.
